title: Modern Web & JavaScript
description: Test your mastery of JavaScript, CSS layout models, DOM, and modern web architecture.

questions.question: Which HTTP status code signifies that a resource has been permanently moved to a new URI?
questions.hint: It is in the 3xx redirection family and specifically marks permanent moves for SEO.
questions.explanation: HTTP 301 indicates that the requested resource has been definitively assigned a new permanent URI.

questions.question: What is the primary difference between 'let' and 'var' in modern JavaScript?
options: 'let' is hoisted to the top of the script and initialized with null
There is no difference in ES6+
questions.hint: Think about code blocks wrapped in curly braces { } like if-statements and loops.
questions.explanation: 'let' declarations are block-scoped (confined to the enclosing pair of braces) and enter the Temporal Dead Zone until initialized.

questions.question: Which CSS property specifies whether an element creates a new stacking context for z-index layering?
questions.hint: It literally contains the word 'isolate' to separate stacking contexts cleanly.
questions.explanation: 'isolation: isolate' creates a new stacking context without requiring position, opacity, or transform tricks.

questions.question: What does the 'defer' attribute on a <script> tag guarantee?
options: The script executes asynchronously as soon as it downloads
The script is downloaded in parallel and executed in document order after HTML parsing
The script blocks DOM parsing until completely loaded
The script only runs when the window triggers the 'unload' event
questions.hint: It defers execution until the HTML document is fully parsed, preserving script order.
questions.explanation: 'defer' downloads the script in parallel without blocking HTML parsing, then executes in order right before DOMContentLoaded.

questions.question: In JavaScript, what is the output of: typeof NaN ?
questions.hint: Even though it stands for 'Not-a-Number', numeric arithmetic produces it.
questions.explanation: In IEEE 754 floating-point arithmetic and JavaScript specification, NaN represents 'Not-a-Number', but its data type is 'number'.

questions.question: Which web API is designed to measure Core Web Vitals such as LCP, FID/INP, and CLS?
questions.hint: It observes browser performance events and timeline entries.
questions.explanation: PerformanceObserver allows developers to listen for and record browser performance timeline entries, including Core Web Vitals.

questions.question: What happens when a Promise is passed to Promise.all() where one of the promises rejects?
options: It ignores the rejected promise and returns resolved ones
It immediately rejects with the reason of the first rejected promise
It waits for all promises to settle before reporting the error
It returns an array containing both successes and errors
questions.hint: Promise.all adheres to a 'fail-fast' mechanism.
questions.explanation: Promise.all 'fail-fast' behavior means it immediately rejects as soon as any promise in the iterable rejects. (Use Promise.allSettled for waiting on all).

questions.question: Which HTML element provides a semantic, accessible native modal dialog box with keyboard focus trapping?
questions.hint: It has methods like .showModal() and .close().
questions.explanation: The native HTML5 <dialog> element provides built-in focus trapping, Esc key dismissal, and backdrop rendering via dialog.showModal().

questions.question: What is the time complexity of looking up a key in a JavaScript Map or Set?
questions.hint: Maps and Sets use hash table backing stores for constant-time lookups.
questions.explanation: JavaScript Map and Set implementations use hash tables providing average O(1) time complexity for lookup, insertion, and deletion.

questions.question: Which modern CSS pseudo-class acts as a parent or relational selector?
questions.hint: It checks if the element 'has' certain child or sibling matches.
questions.explanation: The :has() relational pseudo-class allows styling an element based on its descendants or subsequent siblings.

questions.question: In modern CSS, what does the :has() pseudo-class enable that was previously impossible without JavaScript?
options: Selecting a parent element based on its descendants or following siblings
Creating 3D WebGL meshes directly in stylesheets
questions.hint: Often referred to as the "parent selector" in CSS.
questions.explanation: The :has() relational pseudo-class acts as a parent selector, matching elements if any relative selectors match from that element.

questions.question: Which HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 feature eliminates Head-of-Line blocking at the application stream layer?
options: Multiplexing independent streams over a single connection
questions.hint: Multiple requests and responses are interleaved simultaneously in frames.
questions.explanation: Multiplexing breaks requests and responses into independent binary frames transmitted over one connection without blocking other streams.

title: Science & The Universe
description: Explore mysteries of quantum mechanics, astrophysics, biology, and chemistry.

questions.question: What is the powerhouse organelle of eukaryotic cells responsible for producing ATP?
questions.hint: Famous biology slogan: 'Mitochondria is the powerhouse of the cell.'
questions.explanation: Mitochondria generate most of the cell's supply of adenosine triphosphate (ATP), used as a source of chemical energy.

questions.question: What particle is theorized to give mass to elementary particles through its quantum field?
questions.hint: Discovered at CERN's Large Hadron Collider in 2012; nicknamed 'The God Particle'.
questions.explanation: The Higgs boson is the excitation of the Higgs field, which gives mass to fundamental quarks and leptons via the Brout-Englert-Higgs mechanism.

questions.question: What is the approximate speed of light in a vacuum?
questions.hint: Almost 300,000 kilometers per second.
questions.explanation: Light travels at exactly 299,792,458 meters per second (approx. 299,792 km/s) in a vacuum.

questions.question: Which planet in our solar system has the highest surface temperature despite not being closest to the Sun?
questions.hint: Named after the Roman goddess of love, it suffers from a runaway greenhouse effect.
questions.explanation: Venus has a runaway greenhouse effect caused by a dense atmosphere of 96.5% carbon dioxide, keeping surface temperatures around 465°C.

questions.question: What type of chemical bond involves the sharing of electron pairs between atoms?
questions.hint: The prefix 'co-' signifies cooperation or sharing.
questions.explanation: A covalent bond is formed when two atoms share one or more pairs of valence electrons to achieve stability.

questions.question: What is the event horizon of a black hole?
options: The singularity at the exact center
The boundary beyond which nothing, not even light, can escape
The accretion disk of glowing superheated gas
questions.hint: The point of no return for anything falling towards a black hole.
questions.explanation: The event horizon is the cosmic boundary where escape velocity equals and exceeds the speed of light.

questions.question: What is the most abundant chemical element in the observable universe?
questions.hint: Element #1 on the Periodic table with atomic symbol H.
questions.explanation: Hydrogen accounts for approximately 75% of the elemental mass of the observable universe.

questions.question: Which principle states that you cannot simultaneously know both the precise position and momentum of a particle?
questions.hint: Formulated by German physicist Werner Heisenberg.
questions.explanation: Werner Heisenberg formulated that Δx · Δp ≥ ℏ/2, meaning fundamental limits exist when measuring conjugate variables.

questions.question: What is the theoretical boundary around a black hole beyond which nothing, not even light, can escape?
questions.hint: The point of no return where escape velocity exceeds light speed.
questions.explanation: The event horizon is the outer boundary where the gravitational pull becomes so intense that nothing can overcome escape velocity.

questions.question: What subatomic particle was experimentally verified at CERN's Large Hadron Collider in 2012, responsible for conferring mass to other particles?
questions.hint: Often colloquially termed the "God Particle".
questions.explanation: The Higgs boson is the quantum excitation of the Higgs field, which gives fundamental mass to quarks and leptons via electroweak symmetry breaking.

title: World Geography & Wonders
description: Travel across continents, capitals, mountain ranges, and architectural wonders.

questions.question: Which is the largest desert in the world by total surface area?
questions.hint: Deserts are defined by low precipitation, not temperature; look to the southern pole.
questions.explanation: Antarctica is technically a desert due to very low precipitation, and with 14.2 million km² it is the largest desert on Earth (Sahara is the largest hot desert).

questions.question: What is the capital city of Australia?
questions.hint: It is neither Sydney nor Melbourne, but a planned city between the two.
questions.explanation: Canberra was chosen as the compromise capital of Australia in 1908 to settle rivalries between Sydney and Melbourne.

questions.question: Which river flows through the highest number of countries in the world?
questions.hint: Flowing through central and southeastern Europe, touching 10 countries.
questions.explanation: The Danube flows through or borders 10 European nations: Germany, Austria, Slovakia, Hungary, Croatia, Serbia, Romania, Bulgaria, Moldova, and Ukraine.

questions.question: Which country spans 11 time zones, the most of any continuous contiguous landmass?
questions.hint: The largest nation by total land area on Earth.
questions.explanation: Russia spans 11 consecutive time zones from Kaliningrad on the Baltic Sea to Kamchatka on the Pacific Ocean.

questions.question: What is the deepest known location in Earth's oceans?
questions.hint: Located in the western Pacific Ocean within the Mariana Trench.
questions.explanation: Challenger Deep sits at the southern end of the Mariana Trench at an approximate depth of nearly 11,000 meters (36,000 feet).

questions.question: Which country is home to the historic ancient rock city of Petra?
questions.hint: A Middle Eastern kingdom bordered by Israel, Syria, Iraq, and Saudi Arabia.
questions.explanation: Petra, carved into vibrant red-rose sandstone cliffs, was the capital of the Nabataean Kingdom in southern Jordan.

questions.question: What is the deepest known oceanic trench on planet Earth?
questions.hint: Located in the western Pacific Ocean, reaching roughly 11,000 meters down.
questions.explanation: Challenger Deep in the Mariana Trench plunges nearly 11,000 meters (36,000 feet) below sea level.

questions.question: Which African country is entirely enclaved (surrounded) by South Africa?
questions.hint: A kingdom perched high in the Maloti Mountains, completely enclosed within South Africa.
questions.explanation: The Kingdom of Lesotho is an independent enclave country completely surrounded by the territory of South Africa.

questions.question: Which sea is situated at the lowest land-based elevation on Earth (-430 meters below sea level)?
questions.hint: Hypersaline lake bordered by Jordan and Israel, famous for extreme buoyancy.
questions.explanation: The surface and shores of the Dead Sea sit at 430+ meters below sea level, the lowest land elevation on Earth.

questions.question: What is the only continent on Earth that contains no active volcanic activity on land?
questions.hint: The continent lies entirely within a stable tectonic plate away from boundaries.
questions.explanation: Mainland Australia contains no active volcanoes because it sits stably in the interior of the Indo-Australian tectonic plate.

title: History & Civilization
description: Journey through ancient empires, pivotal revolutions, and historical milestones.

questions.question: In what year did the Apollo 11 mission land the first humans on the Moon?
questions.hint: It took place in the summer of the famous Woodstock festival year.
questions.explanation: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin stepped onto the lunar surface on July 20, 1969.

questions.question: Who was the first Emperor of a unified China and commissioned the Terracotta Army?
questions.hint: His dynasty gave the modern name to 'China'.
questions.explanation: Qin Shi Huang unified the Warring States in 221 BC and founded the Qin dynasty, building the Terracotta Army to guard his mausoleum.

questions.question: What ancient trade network connected East Asia with the Mediterranean for centuries?
questions.hint: Named after the prized lustrous fabric exported from China.
questions.explanation: The Silk Road was an expansive network of Eurasian trade routes active from the Han dynasty through the Middle Ages.

questions.question: The Rosetta Stone was crucial for deciphering which ancient script?
questions.hint: The pictorial script written on papyrus and inside Egyptian tombs.
questions.explanation: Discovered in 1799, the Rosetta Stone contained the same decree in hieroglyphs, Demotic, and Ancient Greek, unlocking Egyptian hieroglyphs.

questions.question: Which invention by Johannes Gutenberg in the 1440s sparked an information revolution in Europe?
questions.hint: Enabled mass production of books, notably the Gutenberg Bible.
questions.explanation: Gutenberg's movable type printing press enabled rapid, affordable dissemination of knowledge across the Western world.

questions.question: Which Roman general crossed the Rubicon River in 49 BC, igniting a civil war and leading to the fall of the Republic?
questions.hint: He uttered "Alea iacta est" (The die is cast).
questions.explanation: Julius Caesar's defiance in crossing the Rubicon into Italy precipitated the Roman civil war and his rise as dictator.

questions.question: The Rosetta Stone was pivotal in deciphering which ancient writing system?
questions.hint: Contains decree inscriptions in hieroglyphic, Demotic, and ancient Greek.
questions.explanation: Discovered in 1799, the Rosetta Stone enabled Jean-François Champollion to unlock ancient Egyptian hieroglyphic text.

questions.question: In what year was the Magna Carta signed by King John of England at Runnymede?
questions.hint: Early 13th century, establishing the principle that everyone—even the monarch—is subject to law.
questions.explanation: The Magna Carta was signed in June 1215, laying foundations for constitutional governance and individual rights.

questions.question: Which ancient Mesopotamian code of laws is famous for the doctrine of "an eye for an eye"?
questions.hint: Babylonian king who inscribed laws onto a giant black diorite stele.
questions.explanation: The Code of Hammurabi (c. 1754 BC) is one of the earliest preserved legal codes, renowned for lex talionis (retaliation).

questions.question: Who was the first emperor of a unified China, commissioned the Terracotta Army, and standardized coins and measurements?
questions.hint: Founder of the Qin Dynasty whose tomb is guarded by thousands of clay soldiers in Xi'an.
questions.explanation: Qin Shi Huang unified the warring states of China in 221 BC, initiating the imperial era and building the first Great Wall sections.

title: Computer Science & Logic
description: Data structures, algorithms, cryptography, and computing milestones.

questions.question: Which data structure operates on a Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) order?
questions.hint: Think of a stack of plates in a cafeteria; you take the one from the top.
questions.explanation: A Stack pushes elements on top and pops them from the top, following the Last-In, First-Out (LIFO) principle.

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of standard QuickSort?
questions.hint: Quadratic time occurs when pivot selection repeatedly splits array into size 0 and n-1.
questions.explanation: When an unbalanced pivot is chosen repeatedly (such as on an already sorted array with poor pivot selection), QuickSort degrades to O(n²).

questions.question: Who is widely recognized as the world's first computer programmer for writing an algorithm for the Analytical Engine?
questions.hint: Daughter of Lord Byron, she collaborated with Charles Babbage.
questions.explanation: Ada Lovelace published the first algorithm intended to be processed by Charles Babbage's mechanical general-purpose computer.

questions.question: In asymmetric (public-key) cryptography, which key is used to decrypt a message encrypted with a public key?
questions.hint: Only the recipient holds this secret counterpart key.
questions.explanation: Data encrypted with the recipient's public key can only be decrypted by the corresponding private key owned exclusively by the recipient.

questions.question: Which algorithm is commonly used to find the shortest path in a weighted graph with non-negative edge weights?
questions.hint: Dutch computer scientist Edsger W. Dijkstra formulated this greedy approach.
questions.explanation: Dijkstra's Algorithm greedily explores nearest vertices to compute the shortest path from a single source in non-negative weighted graphs.

questions.question: What is the time complexity of searching for an element in a balanced Binary Search Tree (like an AVL or Red-Black tree)?
questions.hint: Each comparison discards approximately half of the remaining subtrees.
questions.explanation: In a balanced binary search tree with n nodes, the maximum height is bounded by O(log n), providing logarithmic search time.

questions.question: In relational databases, what does ACID stand for regarding transactions?
questions.hint: Key guarantees for database transactions to remain reliable even in system failures.
questions.explanation: ACID guarantees that database transactions are processed reliably: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability.

questions.question: Which sorting algorithm is asymptotically optimal with O(n log n) worst-case time complexity while also being stable?
questions.hint: Divides the list in half recursively, sorts each, then blends them back together.
questions.explanation: Merge Sort guarantees O(n log n) in all cases (best, average, and worst) and preserves relative order of duplicate elements (stability).

questions.question: What consensus algorithm is famously used in Bitcoin to secure the distributed ledger without a central authority?
questions.hint: Miners expend computational energy solving cryptographic hashing puzzles.
questions.explanation: Bitcoin uses Nakamoto consensus based on Proof of Work (PoW) with SHA-256 hashing to secure transaction blocks.

questions.question: Which famous theoretical computer science problem asks whether every problem whose solution can be verified quickly can also be solved quickly?
questions.hint: One of the seven Millennium Prize Problems in mathematics with a $1,000,000 prize.
questions.explanation: P vs NP is a major unsolved question asking if polynomial-time verification (NP) implies polynomial-time solvability (P).

title: Pop Culture & General Trivia
description: Fun, mind-bending trivia spanning cinema, music, arts, and records.

questions.question: Which film won the first Academy Award for Best Animated Feature in 2002?
questions.hint: Features an ogre, a talking donkey, and a swamp.
questions.explanation: DreamWorks Animation's 'Shrek' won the inaugural Best Animated Feature Oscar at the 74th Academy Awards.

questions.question: How many squares are there on a standard tournament chessboard?
questions.hint: An 8 by 8 grid of alternating squares.
questions.explanation: A standard chessboard has an 8x8 grid of alternating dark and light squares, totaling 64 squares.

questions.question: What was the first music video broadcast on MTV upon its launch in 1981?
options: 'Video Killed the Radio Star' by The Buggles
questions.hint: The title speaks literally about video killing radio.
questions.explanation: MTV debuted on August 1, 1981, playing 'Video Killed the Radio Star' as its symbolic first music video.

questions.question: Which mythical creature is the national animal and symbol of Scotland?
questions.hint: A legendary horse-like creature with a single spiraling horn on its forehead.
questions.explanation: The unicorn has been an emblem of Scotland since the 12th century, prized for its chivalric power and purity.

questions.question: Which artist painted "The Starry Night" while staying at the Saint-Paul-de-Mausole asylum in France?
questions.hint: Post-Impressionist Dutch master known for expressive swirling brushstrokes and sunflowers.
questions.explanation: Vincent van Gogh painted The Starry Night in June 1889 depicting the view from his asylum room window at Saint-Rémy-de-Provence.

questions.question: What is the rarest blood type in the human ABO and Rh blood group systems?
questions.hint: Less than 1% of the global population has this specific Rh-negative combination.
questions.explanation: AB-negative is considered the rarest standard blood type, occurring in less than 1% of people worldwide.

questions.question: Which world-renowned scientist refused the presidency of Israel in 1952?
questions.hint: Theoretical physicist who formulated the theory of General Relativity.
questions.explanation: Albert Einstein was offered the presidency of Israel after the death of Chaim Weizmann in 1952, but politely declined.

questions.question: In literature, what is the fictional surname of the three detective brothers Sherlock, Mycroft, and Eurus?
questions.hint: Created by Sir Arthur Conan Doyle, residing at 221B Baker Street.
questions.explanation: Sherlock Holmes and his elder brother Mycroft Holmes are the famous creations of Arthur Conan Doyle.

questions.question: What is the oldest known musical instrument discovered by archaeologists?
options: Divje Babe Bone Flute (40,000+ years old)
questions.hint: Carved from cave bear femur with spaced finger holes discovered in Slovenia.
questions.explanation: Paleolithic bone flutes, such as the Divje Babe flute (43,000+ years old) and Hohle Fels flute, are the earliest confirmed musical instruments.

questions.question: Which chemical element has the highest melting point of all known metals (3,422 °C)?
questions.hint: Symbol W, historically used as incandescence lamp filament.
questions.explanation: Tungsten (W, atomic number 74) has the highest melting point among all metals at 3,422 °C (6,192 °F).
